overview: Dairen despatch reports military-police surveillance of shortwave-radio sales after the Ling Sheng affair and February 26 Incident, pressing RCA Victor's manager to disclose dealer sales to trace Russian/foreign buyers; the consul notes commercial risks and irony that police themselves urgently needed a powerful receiver for Tokyo news.

people.name: Ling Sheng
people.role: Manchukuo official whose affair prompted heightened police concern

subfiles.title: Despatch on military-police surveillance of shortwave-radio sales in Dairen
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports a military-police demand for information about shortwave-radio sales and considers its implications for foreigners and American radio businesses in Dairen.
subfiles.summary: Dairen police demanded RCA Victor's shortwave sales list after the Ling Sheng affair and February 26 Incident to trace Russian/foreign buyers; the company gave list prices on the consul's advice, ending inquiry. Grummon warns a ban would eliminate American radio business, noting even police increasingly used shortwave.

interest: Shows Dairen police surveilling radio and Russian residents amid insecurity, even using radios during the Tokyo uprising.
